title: Lane A7.1 — Canonical Disclosure Evidence Admission Closure and Query-Service Adversarial Hardening
overclaim_nature: The A7 completion claim asserted that A6 survived claim-adversary verification when the following defects were present in the promoted code

overclaim_detailed.defect_1: No jsonschema validation at _append_transition_event — canonical transition evidence was appended without fail-closed schema admission. Schema compliance was asserted as documentation, not enforced at the append boundary.
overclaim_detailed.defect_2: recover_disclosure_transition() set recovery_detail in-memory on the COMPLETED step but did not persist it through the advance_transition call, making recovery provenance invisible to the ledger and downstream read-side projections.
overclaim_detailed.defect_3: DisclosureQueryResult._seal_result() included generated_at in its digest computation, making projection digests non-deterministic across identical evidence reads.
overclaim_detailed.defect_4: recover_disclosure_transition() read _last_event_for_auth() outside the exclusive transition lock, creating a stale-read race window where concurrent recovery processes could produce duplicate COMPLETED events for the same transition.

changes: Added jsonschema import with graceful None fallback
Added _load_transition_schema() — loads v2 schema from module-relative path, caches, hard-refuses on missing/bad schema
Added _jsonschema_validate() — thin wrapper for pyright type safety

Added _validate_disclosure_event() — content-light structural check for disclosure events (no governing schema published yet for rig.relay.disclosure_event.v1; admission validates metadata and content-light guarantee)
Updated evidence_digest schema pattern from '^sha256:[a-f0-9]{64}$' to '^(sha256:)?[a-f0-9]{64}$' to accept production raw-hex hashes
recover_disclosure_transition() COMPLETED step now passes recovery_detail='recovered_and_completed' through advance_transition() rather than setting it in-memory only
_seal_result() now excludes both 'query_digest' and 'generated_at' from digest computation
Added post-lock re-read of _last_event_for_auth() inside recover_disclosure_transition() to detect competing concurrent completions and return idempotently

test_proofs_exercised: Uninterrupted disclosure with schema-validated append, query service projection
Crash-recovery from AUTHORIZATION_CONSUMED window with recovered_and_completed provenance
Concurrent recovery convergence — one COMPLETED authority, post-lock re-read prevents duplicates
Protected-content S_ string-literal exclusion with production bundle/manifest
Schema admission refusal — wrong schema_version (v1) rejected before append, ledger unchanged
Schema admission refusal — missing required field rejected before append, ledger unchanged
Schema admission refusal — extra property rejected before append, ledger unchanged
Schema admission refusal — invalid transition_id pattern rejected, ledger unchanged
Query service excludes evidence refused at admission boundary
Recovery provenance visible from fresh process reading only the ledger (real subprocess probe)
Query service non-mutation: transition and disclosure-event ledger bytes unchanged after all query operations
Deterministic projection digest over identical canonical evidence
Schema version and content-light guarantee in query output
Original CLI argparse → main() → disclose production path

disclosure_event_authority.explanation: Disclosure events carry schema_version 'rig.relay.disclosure_event.v1' but no governing JSON Schema has been published for this event domain. The append boundary validates metadata completeness and content-light guarantee but cannot perform jsonschema.validate(). If disclosure events are intended as canonical evidence for their domain, a JSON Schema must be published and enforced.
